Document.Paragraph: Build homes near one stop and jobs near another. Bus stops use connected roads. Railway stations use connected rail. Underground metro and elevated metro use their own track layers. Paint tracks with the matching tool.
Stations need workers. Rail and metro need electricity. Terminals offer more capacity than small bus stops. An isolated stop does not serve passengers.
Transport earns fares and costs money to run. The report shows estimated journeys per month, not individually simulated citizens. Covered homes receive an attractiveness bonus.
Use the Transport button at the top right. Select underground or elevated view before removing tracks; the bulldozer removes that layer first and keeps surface buildings.
Document.p: Select or place a stop to see its walking catchment. Each shaded tile is reachable on foot. Water and buildings can block the walk.

On a direct service, workers can take jobs near the destination stop. Residents can also bring back food and goods from a stocked market. Shopping and commuting share available seats, and bus traffic uses road capacity.
Click a crowded stop in City Advisors to find it on the map and see its walking coverage.
